title: Aiming to emerge as a baritone leader; Mulligan and Pepper Adams
summary: He wants to lead small groups, notes Gerry Mulligan as the only baritone leader, and prefers Pepper Adams.

story.theme_name: Still working: current gigs, upcoming projects and plans
story.community_name: What's next: upcoming tours, records and plans

blocks.x: I know you have to get to another gig soon. Any immediate future plans or long term goals for you?

I just want to keep practicing and getting deeper inside this music. It’s funny you know, I’m 54 years old and I feel very committed to getting out there more as a leader. I’ve, up until this point, been a sideman in many different bands. And I really want to get out and start playing quartet and trio and getting out and getting more gigs under my own name so I can emerge as a leader on this instrument. Because there aren’t that many people who are dedicated to just playing the baritone saxophone. And I think in a way you get typecast as a big band player, as a baritone player, I think it’s hard to break out of that, but I’m determined to try and give it my best shot. But as much as I enjoy playing in big bands I enjoy playing in small groups that much more, and so I’m trying to create more opportunities to do that at this point. So that’s something that I feel really strongly about. If you really look at the history of the baritone, there’s really been only one musician and that’s Gerry Mulligan, who’s been able to really make it as a leader.
And a big part of that was his writing, right?

Yeah. And it was also right place right time. And it was also being a good salesman. That’s not to take away from his genius. He was certainly an incredible musician and I can only aspire to be a tenth of the musician that he was, he was really of course very important. But for me, I’ve always thought that Pepper Adams was a more interesting baritone player as such. At least he touched me in a more meaningful way in terms of what I was trying to do on the instrument, and he never really emerged as a leader in terms of being able to tour with his own band. So that’s something that I’m really striving towards at this time is to try and achieve some kind of direction where I emerge as a leader on this instrument. There hasn’t been one in a long time.
